findings.recommendation: Resolve missing inputs or access limitations before relying on affected checks.

findings.recommendation: Evaluate the capacity model together with shared workloads and cgroup limits.
findings.title: Host memory headroom
findings.verification: Read MemAvailable and the service and ancestor limits in this report.

findings.impact: An active service confirms process state only, not synchronization, reachability or historical uptime.
findings.recommendation: Review any inactive or unavailable service observation alongside application evidence.
findings.title: Service state
findings.verification: Read systemd service state and compare with the captured application status.

findings.impact: A process change during capture can mix observations from different lifetimes.
findings.recommendation: Use identity-stable captures for temporal comparisons.
findings.title: Process identity stability
findings.verification: Compare PID and start identity before and after capture without restarting services.

findings.impact: RSS and cgroup values describe different overlapping scopes; file cache is not anonymous heap.
findings.recommendation: Keep each memory component separate and compare like-for-like measurements.
findings.title: Memory accounting
findings.verification: Inspect RSS, memory.current, anon, file and kernel values without summing overlaps.

findings.impact: Ancestor limits can constrain a service even when its own memory limit is unlimited.
findings.recommendation: Review finite limits across the hierarchy before increasing concurrency.
findings.title: Cgroup limits
findings.verification: Read memory.high and memory.max for the service and its ancestors.

findings.impact: OOM and limit events are counters for their cgroup lifetime, not proof of a current incident.
findings.recommendation: Investigate nonzero counters and use valid continuity evidence for new-event deltas.
findings.title: Memory events
findings.verification: Read memory.events and compare only within a verified cgroup lifetime.

findings.impact: A bounded scan may stop early. Observed apparent and allocated bytes are distinct and are not guaranteed reclaimable space.
findings.recommendation: Read completeness, stop conditions and counts before interpreting storage numbers.
findings.title: Storage scan completeness
findings.verification: Inspect worker checkpoints, scan duration and errors; keep files untouched.

findings.impact: A captured synchronization flag is a point-in-time observation; missing RPC data is not proof of synchronization failure.
findings.recommendation: Check verified local status and block progression when synchronization evidence is incomplete.
findings.title: Consensus synchronization evidence
findings.verification: Read the configured loopback status endpoint without changing service state.

findings.impact: OTLP export success or HTTP 200 alone does not prove current samples from this Fibre process.
findings.recommendation: Use a known exporter or metrics file and verify target identity and freshness.
findings.title: Metrics target and freshness
findings.verification: Inspect the configured metrics pipeline and timestamps without guessing ports.

findings.impact: The supported median check requires the right core version, at least 50 successful samples and current target evidence. Fibre endorsement timing is a different measurement.
findings.recommendation: Treat warm-up, unknown versions and stale samples as insufficient evidence, not a pass.
findings.title: Signing latency evidence
findings.verification: Verify signing_latency_median_seconds, successful histogram counts, target and sample freshness; the supported threshold is 0.010 seconds.

findings.impact: Logical occupancy and budget are application accounting; neither equals filesystem usage or staging bytes.
findings.recommendation: Compare verified occupancy and budget metrics separately from measured directory and filesystem bytes.
findings.title: Logical occupancy and storage budget
findings.verification: Confirm the same Fibre target, metric freshness, budget mode and valid nonnegative values.

findings.impact: Services on the same filesystem compete for available space. Different device IDs alone do not prove separate physical disks.
findings.recommendation: Account for other services when evaluating storage headroom.
findings.title: Data filesystem sharing
findings.verification: Resolve service data directories to filesystem identities and verify topology separately.
